Our most popular banana bread is moist, delicious, and absolutely packed with banana flavor. This Allrecipes community favorite will quickly become your go-to banana bread recipe!
Banana Bread Ingredients
You likely already have all the ingredients you’ll need for this banana bread recipe on hand. If not, here’s what to add to your grocery list:

Flour: All-purpose flour gives the banana bread structure.
Baking soda: Baking soda acts as a leavener, which means it helps the banana bread rise.
Salt: A pinch of salt enhances the overall flavor, but it won’t make the loaf taste salty.
Butter: A stick of butter lends richness, moisture, and irresistible flavor.
Brown sugar: Brown sugar sweetens things up and adds a hint of warmth.

regions.text: The Secret to Super Moist Banana Bread

This banana bread is super moist thanks to butter, eggs, and brown sugar (which adds more moisture than white sugar). Plus, ripe mashed bananas have plenty of moisture on their own. Bake the bread until just done to prevent it drying out, and wrap the cooled loaf tightly in plastic wrap or foil to lock in moisture.
I Tried Our 5 Most Popular Banana Bread Recipes and There Was One Clear Winner
Allrecipes / Grace Elkus
Test Kitchen Tips
“This is a no-fuss recipe,” according to culinary producer Nicole McLaughlin (a.k.a. NicoleMcMom). “I love a plain, simple banana bread.” Here are a few banana bread tips and tricks from the expert:

Avoid choosing green bananas. Instead opt for ripe bananas that are yellow with a few brown spots. 
The best and easiest way to mash bananas? With a fork! 
Stir just until the dry ingredients are incorporated. Overmixing can result in dense, tough bread.
Start checking a few minutes early; the bread is done when a toothpick comes out with moist crumbs, not wet batter.
The recipe calls for a 9x5 lo
How to Store Banana Bread

Banana bread will stay fresh for about 4 days at room temperature when stored properly. To keep it moist, place a paper towel in the bottom of an airtight container or zip-top bag. Set the cooled loaf on top, then cover it with another paper towel before sealing tightly. The paper towels absorb excess moisture, preventing sogginess while keeping the banana bread soft. Store in a cool, dry place at
Avoid refrigerating banana bread, as it can dry out more quickly in the fridge.
Can You Freeze Banana Bread?

Yes, banana bread freezes very well! It will keep for 2 to 4 months while maintaining good quality. Wrap the cooled loaf tightly in plastic wrap, then add a layer of aluminum foil. You can also freeze individual slices if you don’t plan to thaw the whole loaf at once. To thaw, let the bread sit at room temperature while still wrapped to retain moisture. Allrecipes Community Tips and Praise

“I’ve made several banana bread recipes here and I always come back to this one,” says SOULWOLF. “ It is a wonderful standard recipe that you can build upon and customize to your liking.  I generally use about 5 medium size bananas but have used a little as three and it still came out good.”

“Simple recipe that never fails,” according to Jheley. “We Love it! It’s now my go-to! I’ve added nuts, vanilla, cinnamon and chocolate chips (not all at once, but as variations just to experiment a bit and they’ve all been great) I’ve also made them as muffins and it literally never fails!”

“This turned out so yummy,” raves Britt Pfaff. “I’m pretty sure this is the recipe I use every year but always forget! The only change I made was adding vanilla extract and walnuts. I doubled the recipe to make two loaves and my 6-year-old daughter loved making it with me!”

2 cups all-purpose flour
1 teaspoon baking soda
¼ teaspoon salt
¾ cup brown sugar
½ cup butter
2 large eggs, beaten
2 ⅓ cups mashed overripe bananas
Directions

Gather all ingredients. Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Lightly grease a 9x5-inch loaf pan.
 Allrecipes / Abbey Littlejohn
 Combine flour, baking soda, and salt in a large bowl. Beat brown sugar and butter with an electric mixer in a separate large bowl until smooth. Stir in eggs and mashed bananas until well blended. Stir banana mixture into flour mixture until just combined.
